# Level 2 delegated acts and ESMA technical material: digests

All five delegated regulations supplement Regulation (EU) 2024/3005. The RTS apply retroactively from 2 July 2026. Verified against the texts in `library/text/L2-*.txt` (23 Oct 2026). Quote from those files.

## RTS 2026/871: disclosure of ESG rating products
Adopted 21 Apr 2026; OJ 28 Jul 2026; in force on the 20th day after publication; applies from 2 Jul 2026 (recital 4 aligns it with Annex III).
Public disclosures (Annex III point 1):
- **Art 3 Rating products**: risks or impacts covered; how double materiality is applied, and other materiality dimensions; E, S, G factors covered and their aggregation; specific issues covered; whether the Paris Agreement and other international agreements are considered, and whether alignment is assessed.
- **Art 4 Methodology**: title and the rated-item types covered; rating validity period; supporting models and key assumptions; **(e) measures to ensure data quality and reliability**; meaning of the rating scale and basis for any relative comparison; **(g) date of latest update and description of changes**; industry classification used; engagement process with rated items and issuers; process for identifying scientific evidence.
- **Art 5 Limitations**: data availability and consistency; completeness, timeliness, accuracy; assumptions, proxies and data estimation.
- **Art 6 Organisation**: ownership chart (parents and subsidiaries); fee-setting criteria; business model and revenue split; main areas of conflict-of-interest risk.
Disclosures to users, rated items and issuers (Annex III point 2; mapping inferred from recital 3):
- **Art 7(1)** methods used to collect non-public data. **Art 7(2)** potential shortcomings of pre-established statistical or algorithmic systems or models.
- **Art 8(1)** methodology revision: process and frequency, conditions triggering revision, stakeholder consultation, **assessment of the impact on existing ratings**, **criteria for a material change**. **8(2)** methodology version number. **8(3)** steps to ensure accuracy and consistency when data are revised.
Not in the text: back-testing; AI-specific disclosures (dropped after consultation; Level 1 AI obligations remain the baseline per ESMA).
Public disclosures follow the prescribed order, with cross-references and hyperlinks allowed. Rated-item identifiers need not be disclosed.

## RTS 2026/872: separation of ESG rating activities from other activities
Adopted 21 Apr 2026; OJ 28 Jul 2026; in force on the 20th day after publication; applies from 2 Jul 2026.
- **Art 1** (all providers carrying out Art 16(1) activities): decision-making and reporting structures keep assessment staff out of those activities; **dedicated workspaces** (physical separation, outcome-based); **annual self-declaration** by assessment staff (existing code-of-conduct attestations can serve).
- **Art 2** (Art 16(1)(d) investment services or (f) credit/insurance): role-based digital access controls; information controls (watermarking, data classification); confidentiality policies; information-barrier training; compliance monitoring; **adequacy assessment at least every 24 months** with management-body oversight of remediation.
- **Art 3** (benchmark providers under Art 16(3)(c), in addition to Art 2): remuneration and performance evaluation of assessment staff not distorted by benchmark conflicts; ratings must "not rely on a mechanistic use of the constituents or output of a benchmark for which the ESG rating provider is the administrator"; document conflicts before contracting with a rated item, its issuer, or an investor with an established client relationship (incl. group).
- Recital 2: monitoring of communications is good practice, not a binding control.

## RTS 2026/1119: information in applications for authorisation and recognition
Adopted 26 May 2026 [C(2026)3334]; OJ 1 Sep 2026; in force the day after publication; applies from 2 Jul 2026.
- Authorisation (Art 1, Annex II): identity and LEI; contact person; legal status; articles of association; ownership and group chart (parents and subsidiaries only); group activities and supervisors; senior management (CVs, criminal-record certificates or self-declaration); team-level staffing (analysts vs methodology, data, IT); market coverage (product description plus number of rated items per product in the EU); rating procedures and **methodologies** (models and key assumptions no longer required in the file); conflicts policies; outsourcing; separation measures; previous ESG rating activities; Annex I document-reference table; signed senior-management letter; machine-readable format (Art 3). Annex IV endorsement; Annex V benchmarks.
- Recognition (Art 2, Annex III): the above plus legal representative and compliance assessment; three years of financial reports and audit or turnover assessment; **CSV list of ratings intended for EU distribution**; third-country supervision and licensing details.

## Delegated Regulation 2026/910: ESMA fees
Adopted 24 Apr 2026 [C(2026)2580]; OJ 30 Jul 2026; in force 31 Jul 2026.
| Fee | Amount |
|---|---|
| Authorisation (EU) | EUR 40,000 (EUR 20,000 for small providers moving to authorisation) |
| Endorsement or outsourcing request | EUR 5,000 each |
| Equivalence registration (non-EU) | EUR 10,000; annual EUR 6,000 |
| Recognition (non-EU) | EUR 40,000 |
| Small-provider registration | EUR 2,000 |
| Annual supervisory fee | ESMA supervision budget share, pro rata to ESG-rating turnover (year n-2 audited, else n-1); paid by end-March; pro-rated in first year; none if authorised in December |
| Small providers (temporary regime) | Annual fee capped at 2% of applicable turnover; micro providers exempt; cap continues 2 years after moving to authorisation |
Only ESMA may charge fees. National authorities with delegated tasks are reimbursed by ESMA.

## Delegated Regulation 2026/904: procedure for fines and periodic penalty payments
Adopted 24 Apr 2026; OJ 30 Jul 2026; in force 19 Aug 2026.
- Independent **investigating officer** issues a statement of findings. The provider may make written submissions, give evidence, propose witnesses and request an oral hearing, with access to the file (use limited to ESGR proceedings).
- The **Board of Supervisors** decides on supervisory measures and/or a fine; late submissions are still considered.
- Periodic penalty payments: statement of reasons and daily amount, with a time to respond; they accrue until compliance.
- Limitation: 5 years to impose (interrupted by notified acts; absolute 10 years plus suspension); 5 years to enforce.
- Fines are held in **escrow** until appeals (ESMA Board of Appeal, CJEU) are exhausted, then paid to the EU budget.

## ESMA Final Report on the RTS (ESMA84-2037069784-1184, 15 Oct 2025): what changed after consultation
Applications got lighter (ownership limited to parents and subsidiaries; team-level staffing; methodology only). Separation became outcome-based: dedicated workspace replaces segregated offices; network segmentation dropped for role-based access; annual self-declaration; 24-month review; communications monitoring only good practice. Disclosures: the prescribed order applies only to public disclosures; cross-references allowed; rated-item identifiers dropped; materiality explained descriptively; new duty to describe engagement with rated entities; scientific evidence described as a process; AI granularity removed; **criteria for "material change" must be disclosed**.

## ESMA Public Statement, 1 Jul 2026 (ESMA84-1427279869-1396)
The Art 2(2)(k) third-party exemption during transition: from 2 Jul 2026, third parties may keep publishing or distributing ratings of providers that notified ESMA, until ESMA decides. **After 2 Nov 2026**, only providers that applied or notified and appear on the Art 14 register; third parties are expected to check the register.

## Draft Guidelines on Endorsement (CP ESMA84-900617762-2699, 29 Apr 2026)
Documentation expected for endorsement applications, mapped to each Art 11 requirement. Level 1 (Art 11(1)(d)) requires endorsed ratings to meet requirements "at least as stringent as" the Regulation's; the CP describes the documentation ESMA expects. Applications can be made with or after authorisation. ESMA aimed to adopt by end-July 2026 and expected applicants to use the guidelines from 2 Aug 2026. **Still at consultation stage as of 23 Oct 2026**: the page (`ESMA-ENDORSE-PAGE`) lists published responses (e.g. MSCI) but no Final Report. Art 29(2) had required the guidelines by 2 Oct 2025.
